title: Bright Faces, Dark Faces, and the Folded Sun

paragraphs.text: The scene of the Last Day continues. A man will not only flee from his brother, but also from his mother and father, and from his wife and children. Every person on that Day will have a matter of his own that is enough to keep him fully busy. The people closest to him in this world will not be able to help him, and he will not even look for them. The ayahs name the people a man is usually closest to, his brother, his mother, his father, his wife and his children, and yet each one of them is left behind. Then humanity will be divided by the look on their faces. Some faces on that Day will be bright, laughing and rejoicing at the good news they have received. Other faces will be covered with dust, and darkness will spread over them. These are the disbelievers, the wicked ones. The contrast between light and darkness on the faces shows the difference between the final outcome of faith and the final outcome of denial.

A new surah begins with a series of shocking events, each introduced by the word "when". When the sun is wrapped up in darkness, and when the stars fall and scatter. When the mountains are moved away, and when she-camels that are about to give birth are left without care. When the wild animals are gathered together, and when the seas are filled with flame. When the souls are paired, and when the baby girl who was buried alive is asked for what sin she was killed. This last image is especially powerful. The question is put to the innocent victim herself, which shows how serious this crime is and how clearly the guilty will be exposed. Each of these events breaks the normal order of the world that people are used to. Things that seem fixed, such as the sun, the stars and the mountains, will lose their place. Even the wild beasts will be gathered together, and the seas themselves will burn. Through this list, the ayahs make the reader feel how complete and overwhelming the change on that Day will be.

hardWords.m: very great and too strong to resist
